transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-30
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Tom Everett (Redwood Partnerships), Samir Kapoor (QuantumFabric - Head Partnerships), Jules Martin (QuantumFabric - Cloud Architect), Eden Cho (QuantumFabric - VP Product), Nora Li (QuantumFabric - Security)

Summary:
Quick partner intro and discovery between Redwood Inference and QuantumFabric (GPU/cloud provider). Goal to explore integration options (referral / resell / co-marketing), technical feasibility for running Redwood Dedicated and Private on QuantumFabric infra, and initial pilot scope for enterprise customer. Discussed latency/cost tradeoffs, dedicated vs hosted, VPC/on-prem, KMS/encryption, and benchmarking requirements. Agreed to a technical deep dive and to exchange security artifacts.

Topics:
- Partnership models (referral, co-sell, managed offering)
- Technical integration surfaces (networking, VPC peering, private control plane, marketplace)
- Performance and cost expectations for LLM inference (batching, quant, kernel selection)
- Security/compliance needs (SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs)
- Pilot and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone thanks for jumping on, uh I'm Lena from Redwood, I'm the AE on partnerships, with me is Marco and Priya from our SE team, Tom from partnerships as well. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:12] Samir Kapoor: Good thanks, appreciate you setting this up. We've been following Redwood's work on inference, excited to see if there's a partnership fit.
[00:00:22] Jules Martin: Hi all, Jules here. We're especially interested in the Dedicated / private deployment story, our customers ask for more control and lower latencies.
[00:00:31] Marco Diaz: Awesome. Quick agenda — we wanted to learn about QuantumFabric's go-to-market for GPU infra, what your typical customers look like, and then dive into technical constraints so we can map Redwood's Dedicated and Private offerings.
[00:00:45] Eden Cho: That works. I'll give a quick overview of our platform and then Jules can jump into infra details.
[00:00:50] Eden Cho: So QuantumFabric is a cloud provider focused on high-density GPU racks, we do both public region clouds and customer-dedicated pods, typical customers are ML startups and enterprise R&D teams. We also have a channel program for partners.
[00:01:03] Tom Everett: Nice — that sounds like a natural fit. From Redwood's side our Dedicated product is reserved GPU pools with an option for a private control plane for enterprise — basically same surface as your dedicated pods but with our orchestration and observability.
[00:01:18] Nora Li: quick question on data flow — when you say private control plane, does any PII or customer data go through Redwood hosted controllers? We have strong data residency and egress requirements.
[00:01:29] Priya Nair: Good callout. Redwood Private gives a customer-managed control plane option — in the VPC/on-prem model the control plane can be run inside the customer's VPC or on-prem and logs can be shipped to their SIEM. We generally support KMS integrations and customers can opt out of telemetry.
[00:01:45] Jules Martin: can you run the full control plane inside our environment? We have air-gapped customers.
[00:01:51] Marco Diaz: Yes, we have an on-prem package for air-gapped deployments. There are a few things that typically require coordination — e.g., model onboarding (large model blobs), kernel optimizations, and update cadence — but technically it's supported.
[00:02:05] Samir Kapoor: Great — from a partnership perspective we want to understand how we could bundle Redwood Dedicated with our dedicated pods, and what certifications or benchmarks you'd need to feel comfortable recommending QuantumFabric to customers.
[00:02:17] Lena Park: Typical ask is a baseline SLO matrix and a set of performance benchmarks on target hardware. We'll also want SOC2 and security docs to show customers. Marco can speak to bench types.
[00:02:28] Marco Diaz: For benchmarks we usually run throughput/latency tests across sequence lengths, cold vs warm KV-cache, and end-to-end latency including network hops. For GPU infra we look at: GPU model, vCPU pairing, RAM, NVMe sizes, and network latency. For quant models we also profile kernel selection.
[00:02:46] Jules Martin: our fleet has A100s and a mix of L40s in newer racks; we also have HBX nodes for memory-heavy models. Any gotchas with those?
[00:02:55] Priya Nair: A100s are common, L40s are fine — there are kernel differences and you can see variance on long sequences. The big thing is packing / batching policy and prefix cache behavior. Also if you're running multi-tenant pods we need GPU isolation and cgroup config.
[00:03:12] Eden Cho: On the business model — are you open to revenue share for referrals, or do you prefer a reseller partner?
[00:03:19] Lena Park: We're flexible. For smaller channel partners we often do referral credits, for strategic partners we pursue co-sell or reseller with joint go-to-market. Tom can take that conversation offline with your partnerships team.
[00:03:31] Tom Everett: Yeah we'll follow up. One thing to surface: our Dedicated customers often ask for predictable per-token costs and tooling to monitor per-route spend. How does QuantumFabric see pricing for inference?
[00:03:42] Samir Kapoor: We typically sell compute as instance-hour; for inference customers want per-inference pricing and we haven't standardized on that yet. Integrating with Redwood's billing primitives could be interesting.
[00:03:53] Lena Park: Redwood can surface token-level cost breakdowns, you can map usage to routes and models which helps with chargebacks and customer billing — we can work with you on SKU alignment.
[00:04:06] Jules Martin: technical — networking wise, can we do VPC peering or private link to Redwood?
[00:04:11] Marco Diaz: Both are options depending on deployment. For Hosted API we have private link integrations in some regions; for Dedicated we'd typically set up an intra-region private network tunnel and peering to the customer's VPC and optionally run the control plane in their VPC.
[00:04:25] Nora Li: encryption at rest — KMS options? We use customer-managed keys for disk encryption.
[00:04:30] Priya Nair: Redwood supports KMS integrations and HSM for keys. For Private deployments you can bring-your-own-KMS. We'll want to exchange key rotation and audit processes.
[00:04:40] Samir Kapoor: On performance, what sort of latency should customers expect on a 4k token request on Dedicated? Ballpark.
[00:04:46] Marco Diaz: Ballpark depends heavily on model variant and batching. For a 4k request on a quantized 70B model on A100s you might see 600–900ms token latency if warmed and well batched, but for small single-stream low-concurrency use cases latency can be higher. We often recommend batching + KV cache for cost efficiency.
[00:05:06] Jules Martin: do you support model variants for fallback? e.g., if high load we want to failover to a cheaper quant model.
[00:05:11] Priya Nair: Yes, smart routing/fallback is built-in — policies can route by latency, cost, region, and automatically fallback to compatible variants.
[00:05:20] Eden Cho: security/compliance — SOC2 is mandatory for some customers. Do you have a SOC2 or ISO report?
[00:05:26] Marco Diaz: We are SOC2 Type II verified — we can share the summary and a compliance pack once we sign an NDA or through our partner sharing flow.
[00:05:34] Nora Li: Great, we'll need to see network diagrams and audit log retention details.
[00:05:39] Marco Diaz: We'll include those in the pack.
[00:05:42] Samir Kapoor: What's the typical pilot timeline? Some of our customers want a two-week proof of concept to validate latency/cost.
[00:05:48] Lena Park: Two weeks is reasonable for a focused bench + validation, but for enterprise-friendly pilots with closed networks and security reviews expect 4–8 weeks including legal and provisioning.
[00:05:59] Tom Everett: Commercially, do you need committed capacity from QuantumFabric to run Dedicated?
[00:06:04] Marco Diaz: For Redwood Dedicated there's an option for reserved GPU pools — customers can commit monthly/annual — but we also have burst capacity and hybrid modes. For a partner offering we could look at a dedicated pool on QuantumFabric with capacity commitments.
[00:06:18] Jules Martin: From infra operations side, how are updates handled for the inference runtime? Rolling updates? Maintenance windows?
[00:06:24] Priya Nair: Rolling updates are default, we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies. For Private/on-prem we coordinate maintenance windows with the customer — binary distribution is controlled.
[00:06:36] Samir Kapoor: A couple of quick pain points from our customers: 1) slow cold-start for large models when cache is empty, 2) hard to estimate per-inference costs across models. Anything here?
[00:06:48] Marco Diaz: Cold-starts are mitigated by pre-warming and prefix caching; we can also snapshot KV caches for common prompts. For cost estimation we provide tooling in Redwood Optimize which recommends batching and quantization profiles to bring costs down.
[00:07:05] Eden Cho: Onboarding models — how heavy is the model transfer? Some of our customers have limited egress windows or want to host models locally.
[00:07:12] Priya Nair: Model blobs can be large — we support streaming model distribution and air-gapped model packaging for on-prem installs. If bandwidth is constrained we coordinate physical transfer or accelerate via pre-shared images.
[00:07:26] Jules Martin: Are there licensing constraints for open models? We sometimes have customers who want to run Llama-like models, need clarity on licenses.
[00:07:33] Marco Diaz: License compliance is on the customer and partner — Redwood maintains a model catalog and flags models with special license terms — we advise and can remove or restrict models per customer policy.
[00:07:46] Samir Kapoor: From a GTM lens, what do you expect from a partner? Technical enablement, co-marketing, deal registration?
[00:07:53] Lena Park: All of the above. Usually start with technical enablement and a pilot reference, then co-marketing and deal registration for joint customers. We can offer training and partner portal access.
[00:08:03] Tom Everett: Great. Jules, on the technical deep dive — can you pull together a representative workload for us to bench? Maybe a chat inference flow plus embeddings?
[00:08:12] Jules Martin: yes we'll put together a short workload profile, target models, and preferred GPU types; aim to get that to you early next week.
[00:08:20] Marco Diaz: Perfect — we'll set up a test plan. Also if you can provide expected concurrency and p95 latency targets it helps shape the test harness.
[00:08:30] Eden Cho: Ok, one more security Q — do you do customer-level audit logs with token-level tracing? Our compliance folks want traceability.
[00:08:36] Priya Nair: Yes, we surface per-request logs and audit trails; customers can export logs to their SIEM. You can also sample payloads for debugging under strict controls.
[00:08:47] Nora Li: retention windows? We typically require 12 months of audit logs for certain industries.
[00:08:51] Marco Diaz: We can configure retention policies; extended retention is an add-on.
[00:08:56] Samir Kapoor: Anything else from Redwood?
[00:08:59] Lena Park: Quick ask — is QuantumFabric open to a co-hosted pilot where we run Redwood Dedicated on your infra for one of your existing customers as a joint reference? That would accelerate GTM.
[00:09:10] Samir Kapoor: Yes, we could identify a candidate customer, but we'll need a commercial outline and an MOU.
[00:09:16] Tom Everett: Ok we'll draft a high-level MOU and partner one-pager.
[00:09:20] Jules Martin: Technical alignment — we'll need to coordinate on network topology and credentials for the benchmark. I'll prepare a network diagram and instance spec.
[00:09:28] Marco Diaz: Great — after the call we'll share a benchmark template and what metrics we capture (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, cold vs warm).
[00:09:40] Eden Cho: timeline for next steps?
[00:09:43] Lena Park: Let's aim for: Lena sends partner one-pager by Tue 2026-08-03; Marco shares compliance pack by Thu 2026-08-05; Jules sends workload and network specs by Fri 2026-08-06; schedule technical deep dive for week of 2026-08-09.
[00:09:58] Samir Kapoor: Sounds good.
[00:10:02] --- End of formal discussion; small side convos, clarifications (transcription continues below) ---
[00:10:12] [00:10:12] Jules Martin: also curious about multi-tenant billing — can Redwood give a per-customer breakdown if we resell?
[00:10:18] Priya Nair: Yes, token-level attribution and per-route cost breakdowns are part of the console. You can export billing CSVs.
[00:10:27] [00:10:27] Samir Kapoor: For the benchmark, we prefer to see both small (<512 token) and long (2k-4k) sequence profiles, please include both.
[00:10:35] [00:10:35] Marco Diaz: noted. We'll include model quantization profiles and a note on expected CPU/gpu ratios.
[00:10:43] [00:10:43] Eden Cho: Are there any preferred telemetry endpoints we should expose for your ops team to pull metrics?
[00:10:48] [00:10:48] Marco Diaz: We expose Prometheus metrics and traces; for private installs we can provide a secure push gateway or allow you to pull.
[00:10:58] [00:10:58] Nora Li: we'll need an NDA before you share the full SOC2.
[00:11:03] [00:11:03] Marco Diaz: Understood, we'll coordinate via Tom.
[00:11:08] [00:11:08] Tom Everett: I'll loop in legal after the call.
[00:11:12] [00:11:12] Samir Kapoor: OK last question: any known issues running on HBX nodes? Some of our memory heavy customers use them.
[00:11:19] [00:11:19] Priya Nair: HBX is less common but we have seen memory-optimized nodes require tuning for KV cache. We'll need to test a specific model and sequence length.
[00:11:29] [00:11:29] Jules Martin: we'll include a model that stresses memory.
[00:11:33] [00:11:33] Lena Park: Great. Any final thoughts?
[00:11:36] [00:11:36] Eden Cho: No, thanks everyone. This was useful.
[00:11:39] [00:11:39] Lena Park: Thanks — recap: one-pager + MOU, SOC2 + compliance pack, workload and network specs, schedule deep dive. We'll follow up via email.
[00:11:48] [00:11:48] Meeting ended at 15:48 PDT

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker overlap and mis-hearings expected; e.g., 'KV cache' rendered as 'KV cash' in auto transcript in places. Some product names abbreviated or slightly off (Redwood Dedicated sometimes shortened 'Dedicated pool'). 

References/shared artifacts mentioned during call:
